title: Reaction after connection
note: Fictional patient. DRAFT pending clinical sign-off. Doses and energies are quoted from the 2025 AHA guidelines (and the ERC where named) for recognition; your unit protocol, crash-cart stock and the attending nephrologist come first. Simulation success is an educational result, not a prediction of patient survival.
intro: Eight minutes after connection with a new dialyzer type, Mr. Romeo Castro, 66, develops hives, wheeze, lip swelling and a pressure of 86/48.

choices.text: Stop the pump, clamp, do not return the blood; call for help; IM epinephrine into the outer thigh per protocol.
choices.feedback: Anaphylaxis: epinephrine first; the circuit carries the trigger.

choices.text: Return the blood quickly to treat the low pressure.
choices.feedback: Returning the blood gives back the trigger.
choices.then: The charge nurse clamps; IM epinephrine is given.

n2.scene: The drug nurse holds a 1 mg/mL ampule and asks, “IV push?”

choices.text: “No. Intramuscular, outer thigh, the protocol dose of 1 mg per mL. IV epinephrine is for arrest, at 0.1 mg per mL.”
choices.feedback: Route and concentration differ; an IV bolus of the IM concentration is a tenfold error.
A bolus of 1 mg/mL IV in a patient with a pulse can cause dangerous arrhythmias.
choices.then: A second nurse reads back the route and corrects to IM.

n3.scene: Despite a second IM dose per protocol, he becomes unresponsive with no pulse.

choices.text: Cardiac arrest algorithm: compressions, IV epinephrine 1 mg every 3 to 5 minutes, isotonic IV fluids (reasonable in anaphylactic arrest), transfer.
choices.feedback: AHA 2025: IV fluids reasonable (COR 2a); the standard IM dose in arrest is of uncertain effectiveness.
In arrest, IV epinephrine within the arrest algorithm and CPR come first.

end.title: 6:40 a.m.
end.text: He regains a pulse and is transferred. The dialyzer, packaging and lot number are kept; that dialyzer type is not used again for him until the physician reviews it.

debrief:
What this case teaches

  • Anaphylaxis: IM epinephrine first; blood not returned.
  • Say route and concentration aloud. IM 1 mg/mL vs IV 0.1 mg/mL.
  • Arrest: the standard algorithm with IV epinephrine and fluids.
